scope: Six closest legal-AI texts, four directly relevant customs/behavioral-testing references, and official task/data/model/software/venue sources; per-reference reading depth is explicit. Not a systematic literature census.

references.title: ContractNLI: A Dataset for Document-level Natural Language Inference for Contracts
references.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2021
references.reviewed: Main task/data, experimental and error-analysis sections; Appendix A.1.1 annotation details
references.supports: Three-way contract NLI with evidence spans; exception/definition difficulty; oracle evidence comparison; not all lawyer-labeled

references.title: Connecting Symbolic Statutory Reasoning with Legal Information Extraction
references.venue: Proceedings of the Natural Legal Language Processing Workshop 2023
references.reviewed: Main data/representation, extraction, reasoning experiments and error analysis; relevant annotation appendices
references.supports: Span-anchored entity/event extraction into Prolog; predicted/partial-gold/empty KB; representation and closed-world ambiguity; four case revisions

references.title: Legal Judgment Prediction: If You Are Going to Do It, Do It Right
references.venue: Proceedings of the Natural Legal Language Processing Workshop 2023
references.reviewed: Main review methodology, data suitability, user/task alignment and recommendations
references.supports: Retrospective judgment facts are not prospective available inputs; task-appropriate legal prediction evaluation

references.title: Performance of LLMs on VITA test: potential for AI-assisted tax returns for low income taxpayers
references.status: published journal article; online publication metadata retained
references.reviewed: Publisher full text via Jina and NSF public PDF; §§2–4 and6
references.supports: 130 IRS VITA questions with260 answer-preserving variants; six models; tax-expert answer construction; numerical answer difficulty; perturbation results do not prove absence of memorization

references.title: Better Call CLAUSE: A Discrepancy Benchmark for Auditing LLMs Legal Reasoning Capabilities
references.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EACL 2026
references.reviewed: §§2–5, limitations and Appendix A.3 human/legal-expert validation; not every prompt in43-page appendix
references.supports: Controlled legal/in-text perturbations, omission/terminology/structural risks, span/explanation/citation evaluation; licensed practitioner reviewed about100 documents rather than entire corpus

references.title: TriBench-Ko: Evaluating LLM Risks in Judicial Workflows
references.reviewed: Main task-risk taxonomy, source construction, annotation and evaluation protocol/results
references.supports: Real-decision-derived task-risk benchmark; three-attorney review including input completeness; differentiated omission, statutory application and overreach risks

references.title: HSCodeComp: A Realistic and Expert-level Agent Benchmark for Hierarchical Rule Application
references.venue: Proceedings of the 64th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
references.reviewed: Official PDF §§3–4 task, data construction, annotation and evaluation; surrounding introduction; not entire32-page appendix
references.supports: Real e-commerce multimodal inputs; US classification rules and CROSS knowledge; target ten-digit code; expert annotation; distinction from supplied-code Section301 scope evaluation

references.title: Explainable Product Classification for Customs
references.venue: ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technology
references.reviewed: Author institution metadata and abstract; publisher full text not obtained in this revision
references.supports: Six-digit customs classification support, explainable output and customs-expert user study; no claim that all methods or limitations were full-text checked

references.title: HSGraphAgent: Knowledge-Graph-Guided Large Language Models for Harmonized System Code Classification
references.venue: Proceedings of the 64th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
references.reviewed: Official metadata and abstract only; no full-text methodological exclusion claim
references.supports: Knowledge-graph and regulatory-exclusion-constrained four/six-digit classification; classification exclusion not automatically additional-duty exemption

references.title: Beyond Accuracy: Behavioral Testing of NLP Models with CheckList
references.venue: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
references.reviewed: Official full text §§1–2: capability matrix, minimum functionality, invariance and directional tests
references.supports: Behavioral input-output relations and task-specific controlled tests; our source audits are an application and provenance extension, not invention of perturbation testing

official_task_and_venue_sources.title: Notice of Product Exclusions: China’s Acts, Policies, and Practices Related to Technology Transfer, Intellectual Property, and Innovation
official_task_and_venue_sources.supports: Published code and product description control exclusion scope; all qualifying importers, not just requester; timing and implementation separate

official_task_and_venue_sources.title: U.S.-China Trade: USTR Should Fully Document Internal Procedures for Making Tariff Exclusion and Extension Decisions
official_task_and_venue_sources.supports: About53,000 exclusion requests2018–2020; request-grant process, not applicability transaction volume; recommendations now closed implemented
Legal AI evaluation/auditing, datasets and original technical/empirical/formal insight within scope
Publisher index list explicitly contains SCIE and Social Science Citation Index
Double-anonymous, editable sources, data availability, actual substantive LLM-use disclosure

official_task_and_venue_sources.locator: 23-page PDF, dated footer; individual note identifiers
